resources.string: Turn your phone into a projector with a box and a magnifying glass.
The lens shows the picture upside down: keep \"Flip top to bottom\" on. Show the focus chart: if the words read the wrong way on the wall, change these settings.

1. A shoebox (or any box), painted or lined in black inside.
2. Cut a hole at one end and fit a magnifying glass or a Fresnel lens (A4 sheet lens, about €5).
3. Lock screen rotation, set the phone in landscape, screen towards the lens, on a support that slides inside the box.
4. Make the room completely dark and point the box at a white wall 1 to 2 m away.
5. Open the focus chart and slide the phone forwards or backwards until the lines are sharp.

• Tap: show or hide the buttons.
• Pinch: zoom. Drag: move the picture.
• Double tap: recentre.
• Keystone: straightens the picture when the box points up or down.
The screen stays on at full brightness.
